'''Carlos Francisco Delfino''' (born 29 August 1982) is an <!--Only Argentine per WP:ETHNICITY.-->Argentine<!--Please discuss on the talk page before changing.--> former professional [[basketball]] player. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], and [[Houston Rockets]]. Standing at {{convert|1.98|m|ftin|abbr=on}}, he plays at the [[small forward]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. He is also noted for his defense and three point shooting skills.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.thestar.com/article/272945 | work=The Star | location=Toronto | title=Laid-back Delfino playing mean 'D' | first=Doug | last=Smith | date=November 2, 2007 | access-date=April 28, 2010}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Early years===
The son of Carlos and Cristina Delfino, he began his professional career playing in the [[Liga Nacional de Básquetbol|Argentine Basketball League]] for [[Olimpia de Venado Tuerto]] in the 1998–99 season, and he then transferred to [[Unión de Santa Fe]] in 1999–2000.

===Italian clubs===
Delfino moved to Italy in 2000 and played four seasons in the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian A League]], the first two with [[Viola Reggio Calabria|Reggio Calabria]] and the other two seasons with [[Fortitudo Bologna|Skipper Bologna]].

In his first season in Italy, he played for [[Viola Reggio Calabria|Reggio Calabria]]. In just under 21 minutes per game he averaged 8.8 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.9 steals. He scored a season-high 25 points in his second game against [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Scavolini Pesaro]], making five of eight three-point attempts. He scored 15 points in just 20 minutes against [[Roseto Sharks|Cordivari Roseto]] and tallied 14 points apiece against [[Fortitudo Bologna|Paf Bologna]], Muller Verona and [[Virtus Bologna|Kinder Bologna]]. He hit at least one three-pointer in 19 of 24 games.

In his first season with [[Fortitudo Bologna|Skipper Bologna]], he moved into the starting lineup in the third game of the season and averaged about 26 minutes. He scored 18 points, including shooting 3-of-5 from three-point range, versus [[Roseto Sharks|Euro Roseto]] and posted double-doubles against [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]] (13 points, 13 rebounds), [[Pallacanestro Cantù|Oregon Scientific Cantù]] (15 points, 11 rebounds) and [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Pippo Milano]] (14 points, 11 rebounds). He suffered torn ligaments in his ankle late in the season, but returned in late May.

===Detroit Pistons (2004–2007)===
Beginning in 2004, Delfino signed to play for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]], who made him the 25th pick in the first round of the [[2003 NBA draft]], making him the first Argentine player ever to be selected in the first round of the [[NBA draft]]. In November 2004, he suffered a knee injury that kept him on the injured list for over three months. He had an operation in the [[United States|U.S.]] and then another in Argentina, where he recovered. However, Delfino did not immediately return to form after his rehabilitation, and was left off the Pistons' [[2005 NBA Playoffs|2005 playoff]] roster. After he recovered from the knee injury, Delfino averaged 15.3 minutes, 3.9 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game in 30 games under coach [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]]. Many regarded Brown as having limited space for Delfino's offensive creativity. It was perceived that under the Pistons upcoming new coach [[Flip Saunders]], that Delfino would thrive.

In his second season on the Pistons' active roster, Carlos averaged 10.7 minutes, 3.6 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.6 assists per game. Delfino played off the bench substituting for either [[Tayshaun Prince]] or [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]]. He had three straight games where he scored in double digits before being sidelined for the next 4 with the flu. Delfino became an important change-of-pace player in Flip Saunders' offensive scheme.

===Toronto Raptors===
On June 15, 2007, the Detroit Pistons traded Delfino to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for 2nd-round draft picks in both the [[2009 NBA draft]] and the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/release_061507.html Raptors Acquire Carlos Delfino From Pistons], nba.com/raptors, Retrieved June 16, 2007.</ref> The 2007–08 season was his most productive in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], as he averaged 9 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game during the regular season.

On June 16, 2009, the [[Toronto Raptors]] extended a qualifying offer to Delfino.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/delfino_release061609.html Raptors Extend Qualifying Offer To Delfino]</ref>

===Khimki===
In the summer of 2008, Delfino signed a 3-year contract with the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Super League]] club [[BC Khimki|Khimki Moscow Region]]. Delfino was one of the highest-paid basketball players in Europe, earning about US$10 million per season, plus a house, a car and a driver, and savings on taxes.<ref>[http://raptorsrepublic.com/blog/2009/07/17/carlos-delfinos-options/ Raptorsrepublic.com Carlos Delfino's options.]</ref> He averaged 13.0 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists, and 1.5 steals per game in [[European professional club basketball system|Europe's secondary level competition]], the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], during the 2008–09 season.<ref>[https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?clubcode=khi&pcode=BCV Eurocup profile and stats.]</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2009–2012)===
On August 18, 2009, Delfino signed a three-year, $10.5 million contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] via sign and trade, the Bucks also received [[Roko Ukić]] in exchange for [[Amir Johnson]] and [[Sonny Weems]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bucks complete trade with Raptors |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks_raptors_trade_090818.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=August 18, 2009 |access-date=2009-08-18}}</ref>

Delfino had a breakout season with the Bucks, as he posted career highs in points per game, rebounds per game, assists per game, steals per game and blocks per game, while playing 30 minutes per game. He also played a major role in the playoffs, shooting a career-high .405 from behind the 3-point line.

===Houston Rockets (2012–2013)===
On August 20, 2012, Delfino signed a two-year, $6 million contract with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/sites/rockets/files/media/delfino_release.pdf |title=Rockets Sign Carlos Delfino |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=August 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120914112358/http://www.nba.com/rockets/sites/rockets/files/media/delfino_release.pdf |archive-date=September 14, 2012 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> After being a starter for three years in Milwaukee, Delfino became the [[sixth man]] for the Rockets in 2012–13. On June 30, 2013, Delfino was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13620 |title=Houston Rockets waive Aaron Brooks and Carlos Delfino |access-date=July 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130827213233/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13620 |archive-date=August 27, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

Delfino's final NBA game ever was during Game 5 of the 2013 Western Conference First Round on May 1, 2013. In that game, Houston would defeat the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] 107 - 100 with Delfino playing for 10 minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 assist. He missed the entire second half due to discomfort in his right foot, which was later found to have a fracture that caused him to miss the rest of the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1628275-carlos-delfino-will-miss-rest-of-playoffs-with-fractured-bone-in-foot |title=Carlos Delfino Will Miss Rest of Playoffs with Fractured Bone in Foot |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=August 2, 2023 |date=May 4, 2013 }}</ref>

=== Injury-riddled seasons (2013-2016) ===
Delfino spent the next three years off the court due to various complications to the injury suffered while playing for Houston, which required nine surgical interventions.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.clarin.com/deportes/basquet/liga-nacional/carlos-delfino-boca-algun-momento-volver-jugar_0_SJk9YLj5e.html |title= Carlos Delfino ya es de Boca: "En algún momento tenía que volver a jugar" |website=[[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]] |access-date=August 2, 2023 |date=March 6, 2017 |language=es}}</ref> On July 17, 2013, Delfino signed a two-year, $6.5 million contract with the Milwaukee Bucks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-free-agent-guard-forward-carlos-delfino Bucks Sign Free Agent Guard-Forward Carlos Delfino]</ref> However, he never appeared in a game for the Bucks during the 2013–14 season due to his broken foot.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/23949197/carlos-delfino-suffers-injury-setback-out-indefinitely|title=Carlos Delfino suffers injury setback, out indefinitely|last=Moore|first=Matt|work=CBSSports.com|date=October 1, 2013|access-date=November 10, 2015}}</ref> On August 26, 2014, Delfino was traded, along with [[Miroslav Raduljica]] and a 2015 second-round draft pick, to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Jared Dudley]] and a 2017 conditional first-round draft pick.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-delfino-raduljica Clippers Acquire Carlos Delfino and Miroslav Raduljica]</ref> Three days later, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-waive-carlos-delfino-and-miroslav-raduljica Clippers Waive Carlos Delfino And Miroslav Raduljica]</ref>

=== Comeback (2016-2017)===
Delfino made his return to the courts in 2016 when he joined Argentina's senior basketball team at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Summer Olympics]].<ref name="rio">{{cite news|url=http://www.cabb.com.ar/web/confirmados-los-12-para-los-juegos-olimpicos-de-rio/|title=Confirmados los 12 para los Juegos Olímpicos de Río|trans-title=12 confirmed for the Rio Olympic Games|language=es|publisher=Confederación Argentina de Básquetbol|date=16 July 2016|access-date=17 July 2016|archive-date=July 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160719045016/http://www.cabb.com.ar/web/confirmados-los-12-para-los-juegos-olimpicos-de-rio/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 6, 2017, Delfino signed with the Argentine team [[Boca Juniors (basketball)|Boca Juniors]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Boca Juniors signs Carlos Delfino|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/228038/boca-juniors-signs-carlos-delfino.html|work=Sportando.com|access-date=6 March 2017|date=6 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307045905/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/228038/boca-juniors-signs-carlos-delfino.html|archive-date=March 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> There, he joined his brother Lucio, who was also recovering from injury.<ref>{{cite news|title=La increíble historia de cómo una medalla dorada terminó siendo un autito de juguete|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes-2/2017/04/01/la-increible-historia-de-como-una-medalla-dorada-termino-siendo-un-autito-de-juguete/|work=[[Infobae]]|access-date=2 August 2023|date=1 April 2017|language=es}}</ref>

On September 27, 2017, Delfino signed with Spanish club [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Baskonia keeps Delfino temporarily|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/885l6fo85yqipaek|access-date=27 September 2017|work=Euroleague.net|date=27 September 2017}}</ref> On October 26, 2017, Delfino finished his stint with Baskonia.<ref>{{cite news|title=Carlos Delfino finaliza su etapa en Baskonia|url=http://www.baskonia.com/carlos-delfino-finaliza-etapa-baskonia/|access-date=25 October 2017|work=Saski Baskonia|date=25 October 2017|language=es-ES}}</ref>

=== Return to Italy (2018–2023)===
On July 3, 2018, Delfino came back to Italy after 14 years and signed a deal with Italian club [[Auxilium Pallacanestro Torino|Auxilium Torino]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Carlos Delfino sings with Fiat Torino|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/279971/carlos-delfino-signs-with-fiat-torino.html|access-date=3 July 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|date=3 July 2018}}{{Dead link|date=June 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On February 27, 2019, Delfino returned to Bologna and signed on the [[Fortitudo Pallacanestro Bologna|Lavoropiù Bologna]].<ref>{{cite web|title=La Fortitudo Lavoropiu firma Carlos Delfino! Venerdì l'esordio in Coppa Italia|url=http://www.fortitudo103.it/la-fortitudo-lavoropiu-firma-carlos-delfino-venerdi-lesordio-in-coppa-italia/|language=IT|access-date=27 February 2019|website=fortitudo103.it|date=27 February 2019}}</ref>

After one year where Delfino didn't play anywhere, [[Jasmin Repeša]], new coach of [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|VL Pesaro]], wanted him in his new team and he was the first hire for the season [[2020–21 LBA season|2020-21]] for Pesaro.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carlos Delfino firma con la VL! |url=http://www.victorialibertas.it/carlos-delfino-firma-con-la-vl/ |publisher=victorialibertas.it |date=7 July 2020 |language=it }}</ref>

On October 8, 2025, Delfino announced his retirement from playing.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Argentine basketball Golden Generation star Carlos Delfino to retire|url=https://buenosairesherald.com/sports/basketball/argentine-basketball-golden-generation-star-carlos-delfino-to-retire/amp|access-date=October 11, 2025|website=buenosairesherald.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Delfino was a member of Argentina's junior national team that won the bronze medal at the 2001 [[FIBA Under-21 World Championship]] that was held in [[Saitama (city)|Saitama]], [[Japan]]. Delfino was also a part of the senior [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentine national basketball team]] that won the gold at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]]. He also played with Argentina's senior national team at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] and at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], where he helped Argentina to win the bronze medal.

In 2011, he won the gold medal in the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship]], held in [[Mar del Plata]].

After years of absence following injury, he played with Argentina's senior basketball team at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref name="rio"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rio2016.com/en/basketball-mens-preliminary-round-group-b-bk-10 |title=Rio 2016 ARG - BRA Men's Preliminary Round Group B basketball game |date=2016-08-13 |website=Rio 2016 official page |access-date=2016-08-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820112226/https://www.rio2016.com/en/basketball-mens-preliminary-round-group-b-bk-10 |archive-date=August 20, 2016 |df=mdy }}</ref>

In 2022, Delfino won the gold medal in the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup]] held in [[Recife]], [[Brazil]]. He was the Argentina's starting [[small forward]] in the tournament
